“The Road North” ~ a beautiful air by Alasdair Fraser

Here’s another way of looking at it in 6/8 time, though 6/4 would probably make more sense ~

T: Road North, The
C: Alasdair Fraser
M: 6/8
L: 1/8

A friend directed me here and to ease my troubled soul I decided to give this some air time and thought… Here’s hoping Alasdair won’t mind his lovely tune being added here. I prefer it much better without the heavy arrangements on the album, but I have been in the minority over such things before… ;-)

I’ve also added this for a newbie to this site, an oboist no less…

Uh oh, where’d I put the transcription in the actual key? :-/

↳ Posted by ceolachan on March 22nd, 2010.

Bb Mixolydian (Bb / Eb / Ab) ~ as heard and first played

That explains it… I first took this off the album in the key I was hearing, which turns out to be Bb Mixolydian. The key I’ve given it in to start will be more friendly for a wider group of instruments, and a half step isn’t a huge move away from what I was hearing. It is possible the recording was sounding a half step sharp, which isn’t anything new. If winds wanted to go there you can follow the above D fingering on an Eb instrument.

I first played and wrote this out in Bb Mix, which isn’t something on this site anyway, when it comes to choosing keys, so I transposed it down a half step to A Mix…

↳ Posted by ceolachan on March 22nd, 2010.

Since there’s no Bb anything here as an option, and for relative keys there’s no c minor, the only option I’d have to give me three flats here would be F Dorian… :-P

For those who would prefer it that half step up, I’ll chase up the transcript and add it here later… I think I laid it down somewhere, maybe the kitchen?

Details

I wonder, if you had it in Bb mix, whether you had a pipe version? There are other details different from AF’s recording, which I’ve attempted to follow below. It’s the first play-through, there’s a bit of jumbling of bars in str 2 on the repeat, all in the spirit of the tune, but defeats the idea of a ‘definitive’ version. FWIW:

X: 1
T: The Road North
C: Alasdair Fraser
M: 6/8
L: 1/8
R: Air
K: Amix
N: Str 2 bars 3, 7 interchangeable on repeat

The Road North by Alasdair Fraser

As transcribed from the album, The Road North, Alasdair Fraser and Paul Machlis. You have to hear him play it to get it. Seen him twice live. Beautiful tone, lots of subtlety and nuance.
